page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B14 processor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled, alongside 16.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, allocating 2.0 GB of memory per core. The processor includes a cache hierarchy consisting of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for advanced vector instructions such as AVX-512 and AVX512_BF16, as well as cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the top 25%. Multi-core CPU performance, Geekbench scores, and Passmark CPU metrics align with the middle 50% average. Text processing shows notable strength, placing in the top 25% of benchmarks. However, memory bandwidth presents a clear tradeoff; while cached read-only bandwidth is average at 566.42 GB/sec, uncached large-block read and write bandwidths fall into the weak and poor categories, respectively, indicating potential bottlenecks for memory-bound workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a dense compute profile suitable for CPU-heavy tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. It is well-suited for workloads such as web serving, software compilation, text processing, and light machine learning inference using smaller models.
